decisions.reason: A newly launched handle family fits the firm's coordinated product system, its tooling and range investment are already sunk, and one year is too early to judge its results.
The mitred family required specific engineering investment and supports the architecture-aware design positioning, so dropping it after one year would expose the launch decision as a mistake.
The multifunctional handle fits the announced barrier-free and system-solution direction, which makes it strategically central and worth keeping despite little visible evidence of results.
This single handle is only mentioned and carries lower investment and commitment, but any weak early results can still be attributed to the launch phase, so the firm keeps it for now.
The collection won the German Design Award, has its own page and is a strong public commitment, so dropping it is very unlikely.
The finish option draws on in-house finishing know-how at low marginal cost and broadens the coordinated range, so there is little reason to withdraw it this early.
